    Rule Settings

    TUNING DESK

    Rule Settings

    Select Apply & Restart to use your changes in a new match. The current match keeps its existing rules.

    The Snowline preset includes 2 Frontline Commands; Emberpact includes 2 Rekindles. Tree-shadow uses 5 copies of each card. The per-card counts below only affect sides using Custom composition.

    Card Stats & Copies · 32 types

    The original custom composition has 12 card types and 30 cards. Counts are adjustable. Cards are drawn without replacement; an empty deck cannot draw. The fixed teaching hand is taken from the deck; generated Inscriptions are not. A full hand skips automatic draws; overflow cards gained through effects go to the graveyard.

    How to Play · Emberpact

    Only the active player may deploy, attack or activate ordinary effects. The other player may resolve triggered effects or use explicitly permitted responses (Runaway Embers ③, Oathkeeper ①). Simultaneous triggers give priority to the active player. At each turn end, all incomplete deployments on BOTH sides are banished without entering the graveyard. Your deployment, automatic draw and attack cooldown timers advance only during your turn. Activated effects continue counting down on either turn.

    Opening-turn protection: During turn 1, no monsters may attack. Normal attacks resume from turn 2. Effect damage is unaffected.

    Attack blocking: If the enemy has any monsters, including deploying monsters, you must attack a monster first. A direct attack is cancelled if a monster appears before impact. Effect damage ignores this restriction. In monster combat, both monsters deal damage to each other simultaneously.

    Wait for the turn timer or select End My Turn. Ending manually requires pending attacks and effects to finish. When time runs out, unlanded attacks are cancelled and all incomplete deployments on both sides are cleared. Switching control changes your perspective, not whose turn it is.

    1. Drag monsters and spells that need no placement target into an empty friendly slot. Drag Inscriptions onto a friendly deploying card.
    2. Placement = deployment begins; Arrival = a monster finishes its countdown. Spells go to the graveyard after their countdown ends; Twin Inscriptions resolves its search first, and Ember Recall resolves its recovery first.
    3. Use Effect Controls to select a card, choose a target and activate an effect. Optional triggers, such as the Apprentice arriving or monsters entering the graveyard, pause the game. Check the effects to activate and confirm; unchecked effects are declined.
    4. Activated effects have an adjustable response window while the clocks continue. Runaway Embers ③ can respond while an enemy effect awaits resolution. A normal attack is not an effect activation.
    5. Once per turn per name is shared by your copies of that card. Once per turn per copy is tracked separately. Numbered effects have separate limits.
    6. Runaway Embers counts only your monsters sent to the graveyard this turn. Echo Furnace listens only to your monsters entering the graveyard; Time Anchor listens only to your monsters being banished.
    7. Time Anchor banks extra time for your next turn if triggered during the enemy turn. Immolating Ritualist ② changes the current turn, regardless of its owner.

    Inscription ② can be activated from the hand via Hand Effects & Recovery. Ember Recall also uses that panel: select a recovery target and pay the displayed Inscriptions to deploy it in the first empty slot. For Oathkeeper ①, select the announced attack to intercept in Effect Controls.

    Tree-shadow · Spell-focused Control & Deck Editing

    The Tree-shadow preset contains 5 spells plus Shadow Recorder, with 5 copies of each. Deploying enemy monsters receive additional deployment time. Deployed monsters have their attacks delayed: cancel their announced attacks, clear attack charges and add time to the existing cooldown, or start a cooldown if none exists. Cooldowns advance only on their owner’s turn. Recorder ③ asks before turn-end banishment. Returning a card to hand instead does not trigger banishment effects or generate Ticks.

    Select Edit Your Deck or Edit Enemy Deck to search, filter, read effects, adjust copies and mix factions. Use 0 to 6 copies of each card, with at least 1 card per deck; recommended size: 30 cards. Saving a named deck assigns it to that side for the next match. Save As and JSON import/export are supported. Decks are stored locally in this browser. The original Tree-shadow cards remain available as Tree-shadow (Legacy).

    Tree-shadow Control (Legacy)

    Select each side’s deck before starting. Redeployment preserves current stats and buffs, cancels announced attacks and clears attack charges. Arrival effects trigger again, with a fresh first-attack delay. Redeployment is not placement or leaving the field. Both sides’ incomplete deployments are still banished at turn end. Optional turn-end effects pause immediately after the turn switches; usage counts belong to the turn that just ended. Delay Edict ② can respond to enemy acceleration without negating it. For Reversion Officer ①, choose the banishment cost → enemy target in Effect Controls.

    Snowline

    Scout searches for a monster when returned to hand and can return any deployed monster after arrival. Shieldbearer may be discarded during the enemy turn to prevent new attacks this turn; already announced attacks still resolve. It searches for a Snowline spell when returned to hand. Field Medic can return another deployed friendly Snowline monster when it returns to hand, healing your hero for 3. Battleworn Swordsman deploys in 15s and spends all Resolve to grant ATK. Against lethal battle damage, it may spend 2 Resolve to survive at 1 HP, without a separate per-turn limit.

    Spellblade Breaker deploys in 25s. On placement it returns all other cards on both fields to hand. After arrival it may destroy an enemy card or negate an activated effect. Negation is once per stay on the field and resets on re-entry. The targeted effect waits for the negation response; costs are not refunded. A monster rescued by Relief Horn may be deployed again this turn. Breaker ① ignores the hand limit for forced returns; excess cards remain temporarily, but ordinary draws still obey the limit.

    Tactical Pause

    Every turn starts in Tactical Pause (except dual-AI spectating). You can also pause using the button or Space. Free-timing effects have manual buttons without automatic prompts. Drag multiple cards into empty slots to plan deployment; Inscriptions can target planned cards. Effects and attacks can also be queued, but cannot spend cards not yet generated or attacks still on cooldown. On resume, all actions execute sequentially at the same game instant. Undo removes the last action; clearing the plan spends nothing. Default mode is player versus AI, AI vs AI spectating uses ordinary pause only.

    Try This Combo

    Deploy Echo Furnace → Deploy Apprentice to gain Quickening Inscription → Use Furnace ① to destroy the deploying Apprentice → Its graveyard entry triggers Furnace damage → Choose Apprentice ③ to banish it and gain Delaying Inscription → Use Delaying Inscription to extend a core spell’s deployment. With Time Anchor on the field, banishing the Apprentice also extends your turn.

    The default response window is 1s; the optional-choice timer is 6s. These are prototype parameters. Effect costs are paid immediately. Activated effects usually persist after their source leaves the field; effects changing their own deployment need the source to remain deploying.

    Trigger Timing · Choose Effects to Activate

    Both clocks, attacks and AI are paused. Check optional effects and choose their targets; unchecked effects are declined. If several effects remain, choose their activation order next. The last activated resolves first. Mandatory effects cannot be cancelled.

    Choose Activation Order

    Use the arrows: the top effect activates first, the bottom last. Resolution is reversed: the last activated effect resolves first.Both clocks and AI are frozen while choosing.

    Resolution Order

    Order the chosen and mandatory effects here. Optional effects were confirmed in the previous step. Even a single mandatory effect pauses for review. The active player has priority.

    Deck Editor

    Save your edits, then start a new match. Each side can use a different saved deck. Mixing factions is allowed.
